[DXVK ≤3.1.1 | dxvk-low-latency (default False) | dxvk-gplasync-lowlatency (default True)] Latency sleep / Reflex. Auto: Reflex only in D3D11 games that use it, with VK_NV_low_latency2 + dxvk-nvapi. True: DXVK's built-in latency reduction for every game (no effect with in-game/external limiters). False: disable both. Removed on DXVK master (after 3.1.1); use dxvk.enableNvLowLatency2 there.

[DXVK ≤3.1.1 | dxvk-low-latency | dxvk-gplasync-lowlatency] Latency-sleep heuristic tolerance in µs. Higher = more latency, maybe smoother pacing. No effect when VK_NV_low_latency2 is used. Removed on DXVK master (after 3.1.1).

[DXVK ≤3.1.1 | dxvk-low-latency | dxvk-gplasync-lowlatency] Don't use VK_NV_low_latency2 (Reflex unavailable; latencySleep=True then uses the custom algorithm). Auto disables it for 32-bit games only. Removed on DXVK master (after 3.1.1); replaced by dxvk.enableNvLowLatency2.
Frame rate limit (0 = off). DXVK 3.x replacement for DXVK_FRAME_RATE.
Enforce stricter max frame latency (0 = app value, 1-16).
Override Vsync for D3D10/11/12: 0 = off, n = on (every n-th vblank), -1 = app.
Override Vsync for D3D9: 0 = off, n = on, -1 = app.
True: mailbox when in-game Vsync is off (no tearing). False: FIFO_RELAXED when Vsync is on (tears instead of stuttering below refresh).
[DXVK master, after 3.1.1 | dxvk-low-latency | d7vk] Present-timing features (non-native refresh emulation, frame limiter). Default True; disable only for debugging.
Only expose display modes with this refresh rate (0 = off). Use with caution.
Auto: GPL + optimized pipelines in background. True: GPL only. False: off (more stutter). Debug option.
VK_EXT_descriptor_heap. Auto: known-good drivers only. True: force if supported.
VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer (descriptor heap takes precedence when both are on).
Pipeline compiler threads (0 = all cores). Lower it to cut compile-time CPU contention on high-core CPUs.
Report NVIDIA GPUs as AMD. Auto hides unless NVAPI is enabled in Proton — set False when you need DLSS/Reflex via dxvk-nvapi.
VK_NVX_* CUDA-interop extensions required for DLSS (default True on 64-bit NVIDIA).
Hide the iGPU when a dGPU exists. Prefer DXVK_FILTER_DEVICE_NAME if possible.
Override reported VRAM in MB (0 = off). Fixes texture streaming in games that mis-handle large VRAM. Not a hard cap.
Expose the HDR10 colour space (defaults to DXVK_HDR).
Force AF for all D3D11 samplers (0-16, -1 = app). Can break bilinear-dependent passes.
Force AF for all D3D9 samplers (0-16, -1 = app).
Add to the app's mip LOD bias (-2.0 .. 1.0). Negative = sharper + shimmer.
Clamp negative LOD bias to 0 (after samplerLodBias).
Legacy per-API D3D10/11 frame limiter (0 = off). Prefer dxvk.maxFrameRate, or MangoHud / Gamescope limiters, which pace better.
Legacy per-API D3D9 frame limiter (0 = off). Prefer dxvk.maxFrameRate or an external limiter.
Enforce stricter max frame latency for D3D9 (0 = app value).
Report AMD GPUs as NVIDIA GPUs (workaround for AMDAGS / AMD-specific code paths). Auto = only for known-affected games.
Report Intel GPUs as AMD GPUs (workaround for Intel-specific libraries such as XeSS). Auto = known-affected games; defaults to True for D3D8/9.
Report NVIDIA GPUs running on NVK (Mesa) as AMD GPUs. Irrelevant with the proprietary NVIDIA driver.
Report this PCI vendor ID (hex) instead of the real one. 10de = NVIDIA, 1002 = AMD, 8086 = Intel.
Report this PCI device ID (hex) instead of the real one.
Report this adapter description string instead of the real GPU name.
Override reported shared system memory in MB (0 = off). Companion of dxgi.maxDeviceMemory; not a hard cap.
Only expose Vulkan devices whose name contains this string. Config-file equivalent of DXVK_FILTER_DEVICE_NAME.
Unreal Engine 4 HDR workarounds for games not named *-Win64-Shipping.exe (avoids AMDAGS crashes in D3D11 on HDR systems).
Cap the D3D11 feature level a device can be created with (default 12_1). Raising it can unblock apps that fail device creation.
Cap the tessellation factor (8-64, 0 = off). Big win in tessellation-heavy games.
Relax UAV pipeline barriers (ignore WAW in compute, all UAV hazards in graphics). Can raise performance; may cause rendering glitches.
Like relaxedBarriers but only for graphics-shader UAVs (compute untouched).
Insert barriers after group-shared-memory writes in compute shaders. Workaround for games with missing GroupMemoryBarrier; costs performance.
Insert barriers after UAV writes in compute shaders. Workaround for missing UAV sync; costs performance.
Per-sample instead of per-pixel shading when MSAA is on. Cleaner image, big performance cost.
Per-sample shading when MSAA is on (D3D9). Cleaner image, big performance cost.
Force every texture to 1 sample and fix up resolves/shaders. Big FPS gain at the cost of no MSAA.
Don't map dynamic images directly. Fixes corruption in games that ignore the driver's row pitch.
Put dynamic resources with these bind flags in cached system memory for fast CPU readback (v=vertex, i=index, c=constant, r=shader resource ...). Buggy-app workaround.
Advertise native driver command-list support (default True). Turn off if a game misbehaves with deferred contexts.
Force-enable the D3D11 context lock (ID3D10Multithread). Race-condition debugging.
Add to the app's mip LOD bias for D3D9 samplers.
Clamp negative D3D9 LOD bias to 0 (after samplerLodBias).
x*0 floating-point quirk emulation. True = fast/less exact, Strict = slow/exact, False = off. Auto = per-game.
Stream shader constants into VRAM; may help GPU-bound scenes. Auto = discrete GPUs only.
Fast-path clears that nearly cover the whole render target.
Initial value (MB) for GetAvailableTextureMem tracking. Raise for old games that refuse to start with 'too little' video memory.
Only expose D3D9 display modes with this refresh rate (0 = off).
Always use seamless cube maps (prettier edges, deviates from real D3D9).
FP16 for partial-precision instructions. May help weak GPUs, can regress desktop GPUs.
Allocate write-only D3DPOOL_DEFAULT buffers in cached system memory (buggy-app readback fix).
Force the aspect ratio of exposed D3D9 display modes.
Cap the VRAM DXVK will use, in MB (0 = off). Debug only: severe slowdown when hit.
Zero mapped memory when suballocations are freed. Huge CPU cost; last resort for games that don't initialise their buffers.
Raw/structured buffer views via SSBOs. Auto = on where offset alignment is 4 B (AMD). Unsafe on hardware with stricter alignment.
Use VK_NV_raw_access_chains on NVIDIA (default True). Disabling reduces performance; debug only.
Resolve multisampled images when a game samples them as plain textures (fixes striped artifacts on NVIDIA). Default True.
Use VK_KHR_unified_image_layouts where available. Default True; debug only.
Free pipeline libraries aggressively to save memory/address space. Auto = 32-bit games only.
Custom sin/cos approximation. Auto = only on drivers with poor native precision.
Tiler (mobile GPU) submission heuristics. For perf testing only.
[DXVK master, after 3.1.1 | d7vk] Use VK_NV_low_latency2 for the Reflex implementation. Auto = on, except in 32-bit games (frame pacing problems). Replaces dxvk.disableNvLowLatency2.
Let the Vulkan driver opt in to exclusive fullscreen on Windows (needed there for VRR/HDR; breaks alt+tab and games with extra GDI windows). No effect on Linux.
HUD elements, same syntax as DXVK_HUD. Ignored when DXVK_HUD is set.
Create the Vulkan surface on the first Present instead of at swap chain creation. For games that start rendering with another API and otherwise stay black.
Expose DirectComposition swap chains backed by a dummy window. Not a real implementation: some games need it to exist, others need creation to fail.
Emit the same Vulkan commands for the same D3D11 commands on every run. For comparative benchmarking; can cost performance and break games that misuse queries.

[DXVK master, after 3.1.1 | d7vk] Report displays on the same Vulkan device as one D3D9 adapter group and allow D3DCREATE_ADAPTERGROUP_DEVICE multi-head devices. Default True; no effect if d3d9.enumerateByDisplays is off.
Reject Device::Reset while losable resources (state blocks, extra swap chains, D3DPOOL_DEFAULT) are alive, as D3D9 does. Default True; False for games that leak them and hang.
D3D9: report this PCI vendor ID (4-digit hex).
D3D9: report this PCI device ID (4-digit hex).
Same as dxgi.deferSurfaceCreation, for D3D9 swap chains.
Return D3DERR_DEVICELOST when a fullscreen D3D9 game loses focus, as Windows does. Some games rely on seeing it, others mishandle it.
Disable A8-format render targets (The Sims 2 workaround).
Call SetProcessDPIAware on device creation (default True), avoiding upscaling blur on Hi-DPI displays.
Enumerate D3D9 adapters per display (Windows behaviour, default True) instead of per physical GPU. May help PRIME setups.
Add and copy a second buffer every frame so GetFrontBufferData works with single-buffer swap chains. Only needed by Silent Hill 2 Enhanced Edition.
Force sampler-type specialization constants; fixes old games that pair mismatched image/sampler types (Halo: CE, Spellforce).
D3D9: report AMD GPUs as NVIDIA (AMDAGS / AMD code-path workaround). Auto = known-affected games.
D3D9: report Intel GPUs as AMD. Defaults to True for D3D8/9 to avoid early-Intel iGPU restrictions.
D3D9: report NVIDIA GPUs as AMD. Auto = only games known to misbehave with NVAPI / NVIDIA code paths.
D3D9: report NVIDIA GPUs running on NVK (Mesa) as AMD.
Ignore the lock range of D3DPOOL_DEFAULT buffers and mark the whole buffer dirty, for games that pass wrong ranges. May cost performance.
Memory-tracking test mode for GetAvailableTextureMem (see d3d9.maxAvailableMemory). Debug option.
List only the desktop mode plus a few fallback resolutions, for games that fail when too many modes are reported (AquaNox 1/2). Combine with d3d9.forceAspectRatio / forceRefreshRate.
Shader model reported in the device caps: 0 = fixed-function only, 1-3 = SM1-SM3 (default 3). Capped to 1 for D3D8 games.
Allow depth formats on cube textures like old drivers did. Some games crash without it (SimCity Societies: Destinations), others break with it (Gothic 3).
Expose the AMD/Intel DF floating-point depth formats (default True). Ignored on NVIDIA or when spoofing NVIDIA.
Support the X4R4G4B4 format (default True; The Sims 2).
Virtual memory (MB) for locked D3D9 textures, 0 = no limit. Does not change real memory use or texture quality; upstream advises leaving it alone.
Use D32F for D24 depth formats, to reproduce AMD issues on other hardware. Debug option.
Draw call batcher for D3D8 games that issue many tiny, similar draws. May hurt performance or cause artifacts elsewhere.
Honour D3DLOCK_DISCARD only for DYNAMIC+WRITEONLY buffers and map WRITEONLY buffers directly, as some old games expect. Costs performance.
Override the vertex shader declaration with D3DVSDE_REGISTER:D3DVSDT_TYPE pairs, for games that read undeclared inputs.
Put P8 (palettized) textures in D3DPOOL_SCRATCH so creating them always succeeds, for old games that don't handle missing P8 support.
Scale the depth texcoord (Dref) from [0..2^bits-1] back to [0..1] for early D3D8 games; the value is the bit depth (typically 24). 0 = off.
Force D3DTTFF_PROJECTED when a depth texture is bound to stage 0, emulating GeForce 3/4 shadow-map behaviour some old games expect.
[dxvk-low-latency | dxvk-gplasync-lowlatency | DXVK-Sarek] Config-file form of DXVK_FRAME_PACE (the env var wins). See DXVK_FRAME_PACE for the modes and each fork's default.
[dxvk-low-latency | dxvk-gplasync-lowlatency | DXVK-Sarek] Fine-tunes low-latency pacing in µs (-10000..10000): positive starts frames later (slightly more responsive), negative earlier (more fps).
[dxvk-low-latency | dxvk-gplasync-lowlatency] Allow a frame to start before the CPU part of the previous one has finished (default True). False may feel snappier but can cost fps.

[dxvk-gplasync-lowlatency] Async pipeline compilation (default True): the main thread is not blocked by pipeline compiles, at the cost of brief glitches while shaders compile. DXVK_ASYNC=0/1 overrides it.
[dxvk-gplasync-lowlatency] State-cache fixes that let Async and GPL work together or separately (default True). DXVK_GPLASYNCCACHE=0/1 overrides it.
[dxvk-gplasync-lowlatency] Allocate only minImageCount swap chain images (double buffering) instead of minImageCount + 1: up to about one frame less latency.
